title: Simplest Form
short: Divide top and bottom by a common factor to use fewer, larger pieces.
trouble: Children divide the numerator and denominator by different numbers.

blocks.html: You can make equivalent fractions by multiplying. Going the other way, dividing the top and bottom by a common factor, uses fewer, larger pieces.

A fraction is in simplest form when the only number that divides both the numerator and the denominator is 1. To simplify $\dfrac{8}{12}$, divide both by a common factor: $\dfrac{8 \div 4}{12 \div 4} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Dividing undoes the cutting. In $\dfrac{8}{12}$, put every 4 small pieces back together into one bigger piece. 12 pieces become 3, and the 8 shaded pieces become 2. Same amount, bigger pieces: $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

blocks.name: fractionbar
blocks.cap: $\dfrac{6}{8}$ and $\dfrac{3}{4}$ shade the same length. Joining pieces in pairs turns eighths into fourths.

blocks.title: One step
steps: Only 1 divides both 3 and 4, so stop.

blocks.title: More than one step
steps: Using the greatest common factor, 6, gets there in one step: $\dfrac{12 \div 6}{18 \div 6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

blocks.html: Dividing the top and bottom by different numbers, like $\dfrac{6}{8} \to \dfrac{3}{2}$ (top ÷ 2, bottom ÷ 4). That changes the amount: $\dfrac{3}{2}$ is more than a whole. Use one number for both, and check that the new fraction is about the same size.
